- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3), model underestimates; adjust upward to reflect bearish sentiment’s fading or reversal.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon (especially days 1–5) when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — apply downward bias to first 5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overreacts and forecasts continued rise — cap forecast at 1–2 days above true peak, then allow mean reversion.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.5 → -0.5 → +0.5), model tends to lag — adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with sentiment momentum.
- When sentiment is flat or mixed (±0.2), model often drifts toward historical mean — apply mean-reversion correction if price deviates >1.5σ from recent 7-day average.
- For 30-day forecasts, avoid extrapolating from 18-day history — use sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 70% recent, 30% sentiment) to reduce overfitting to short-term noise.
